options.label: Graphics backend
options.description: How DuckStation draws the game. Vulkan is usually fastest; OpenGL is the fallback. Software is the most accurate but ignores the internal resolution and the widescreen hack.

options.label: Internal resolution
options.description: Draws the 3D picture at a higher resolution for a sharper image. Higher settings cost speed. Automatic picks the step that fits the screen.

options.label: Aspect ratio
options.description: The shape of the picture. Game's own is the PlayStation's 4:3; pick 16:9 (or wider) with the widescreen hack to draw a wide scene, or Stretch to fill the screen.

options.label: Screen filter
options.description: How the picture is enlarged to the screen. Sharp keeps pixels crisp, Smooth blends them; the 'whole steps' choices only enlarge by whole multiples (integer scaling), leaving borders.

options.label: Widescreen hack
options.description: Draws more of the 3D scene on the sides to fill a wide screen. Only has an effect with a wide aspect ratio (16:9 or wider, or Stretch). Some games show glitches at the edges; DuckStation turns it off for games known to break.

options.label: VSync
options.description: Syncs frames with the screen to avoid tearing. Turning it off can help a slow game but may tear.

options.label: Show FPS
options.description: Shows the frames per second on screen while you play.

notes: Verified against stenzek/duckstation tag v0.1-11894 (c66b269). Every key below is read from ~/.local/share/duckstation/settings.ini (the base layer) by Settings::Load (src/core/settings.cpp) when DuckStation starts; with -batch every game is a fresh process, so a patch before launch is always seen. A per-game ~/.local/share/duckstation/gamesettings/<serial>.ini, when the player made one in DuckStation, is a layer above it and wins for any key it holds (System::GetGameSettingsPath, src/core/system.cpp:1391-1397).

DuckStation saves settings.ini only when a setting changes in its UI (QtHost::QueueSettingsSave/SaveSettings, src/duckstation-qt/qthost.cpp:3217-3255; INISettingsInterface saves only when dirty, src/util/ini_settings_interface.cpp:28-32, 380-414); it does not rewrite the file at exit and never writes its defaults into it. When it does save it re-serialises the whole file as 'key = value' (src/util/ini_settings_interface.cpp:279), quoting only values with # or ; (:255-258), hence separator ' = ' and unquoted values here.
Booleans are written true/false (StringUtil::ToChars<bool>, src/common/string_util.cpp:396-400) and read as true/yes/on/1/enabled or false/no/off/0/disabled (:376-394).

renderer: [GPU] Renderer (src/core/settings.cpp:303-304) is a name from s_gpu_renderer_names (:1574-1589): Automatic, Vulkan, OpenGL, Software on Linux (ENABLE_OPENGL and ENABLE_VULKAN default ON, CMakeModules/DuckStationBuildOptions.cmake:8-9; only the macOS build turns OpenGL off). Automatic picks Vulkan unless the Vulkan driver is a software one, then OpenGL (src/util/gpu_device.cpp:323-325). An unknown name falls back to Automatic (settings.cpp:304). The seed sets Vulkan. Gamedb trait ForceSoftwareRenderer overrides it for some games (src/core/game_database.cpp:663-669).

resolution: [GPU] ResolutionScale is an integer multiple of native, 0 = automatic from the window size (src/core/settings.cpp:306-307, src/core/system.cpp:1058); max MAX_RESOLUTION_SCALE = 32 (src/core/gpu.h:34), limited by the GPU's texture size in the UI (src/duckstation-qt/graphicssettingswidget.cpp:830-864, whose labels name 3x for 720p and 5x for 1080p). We offer Automatic and 1x-5x (5x already covers a 1080p panel); 6x and above stay reachable in DuckStation's own menu. The hardware renderers only: Software ignores it. Gamedb trait DisableUpscaling forces 1x (game_database.cpp:751-763).

aspect: [Display] AspectRatio is a string parsed by Settings::ParseDisplayAspectRatio (src/core/settings.cpp:2043-2073, read at :373-374): the special names 'Auto (Game Native)', 'Stretch To Fill' (Linux; Android writes 'Auto (Match Window)'), 'PAR 1:1', else 'N:D'. All of DuckStation's predefined ratios are offered (Settings::GetPredefinedDisplayAspectRatios, :2109-2116). Default Auto (src/core/settings.h:240).

widescreen_hack: [GPU] WidescreenHack (src/core/settings.cpp:357, written back from gpu_widescreen_rendering at :747) makes the GTE widen the 3D projection to the display aspect ratio (System::UpdateGTEAspectRatio, src/core/system.cpp:6261-6290): with aspect 'Game's own' or 'Square pixels' there is no correction, so the hack only does something with 16:9 (or another wide ratio, or Stretch). The two options stay independent (each writes its own key); the plugin description says to pair them. DuckStation's own hotkey toggle swaps both at once (system.cpp:6163-6194) but only for the running session. Gamedb trait DisableWidescreen and cheat metadata turn it off for known-broken games (src/core/game_database.cpp:799-806, src/core/cheats.cpp:264-267).

smoothing: [Display] Scaling (src/core/settings.cpp:387-389) is one enum that holds both the filter and integer scaling: Nearest, NearestInteger, BilinearSmooth (default, src/core/settings.h:244), BilinearHybrid, BilinearSharp, BilinearInteger, Lanczos (s_display_scaling_names, settings.cpp:2221-2223); the *Integer modes turn on integer scaling (Settings::IsUsingIntegerDisplayScaling, settings.h:219-223; src/core/video_presenter.cpp:609). All seven are offered.

integer_scale left out as a separate option: DuckStation has no integer-scaling key of its own, it is part of [Display] Scaling, so an integer_scale option would write the same key as smoothing and the two would overwrite each other. The integer choices are in the Screen filter list instead ('whole steps'). [Display] Scaling24Bit (FMV scaling, settings.cpp:390-392, used for 24-bit video frames at video_presenter.cpp:915) is left alone: FMVs keep DuckStation's own setting (default Bilinear Smooth).
vsync: [Display] VSync, default false (src/core/settings.cpp:419). show_fps: [Display] ShowFPS, default false (settings.cpp:429), DuckStation's own on-screen counter.

[Main] DisableAllEnhancements = true (settings.cpp:281) overrides resolution (forced 1x) and the widescreen hack (forced off) whatever these options say (Settings::ApplySettingRestrictions, src/core/settings.cpp:1137-1161). RetroForge does not set it; a player who turned it on in DuckStation gets native resolution and no widescreen.

Settings are only read from the file: DuckStation has no per-run command-line override for them, and an unknown command-line flag makes it print an error and quit, so every option here is a file patch.
